assessment: The incumbent provides staffed key access and telephone/in-person booking; eleven groups obtained weekly bookings (H4-O1). Its strongest plausible account is predictable recurring access with modest coordination resources. Success is unproven: needs and acceptable alternatives were not recorded, three access conflicts occurred, and administration averaged 127.5 minutes weekly (H4-O3/O4/O6/O7). The concrete limiting observation is H4-O5: the only piano is in one room, while most equipment entries are blank. Thus 68% aggregate reservation utilization (H4-O2) cannot establish that refused requests could use spare capacity. Evening concentration and missed starts suggest distinct possible constraints, not established causes.

openings.claim: Would recording complete acceptable windows, rehearsal duration needs and necessary equipment reveal a feasible allocation that inherited 90-minute bookings conceal?
openings.delta: Distinguish scheduling rigidity from genuine scarcity of compatible room-time, while counting unmet needs rather than successful reservations alone.
openings.prediction: If inherited times or durations constrain access, a flexible allocation will meet more stated needs with identical resources. If compatible demand exceeds supply, unsatisfied requests will remain concentrated in overlapping equipment/time requirements.
openings.probe: Use each contact's short conversation to record needs, acceptable windows and equipment. Construct a shadow eight-week schedule using two rooms, existing staffed hours and equipment, preserving both performances and each requested weekly 60-minute entitlement. Compare feasible coverage under inherited bookings versus movable bookings; do not implement an infeasible allocation or count outside rehearsals as building provision.
assumptions: Contacts can describe group requirements accurately.
Changing inherited reservations requires agreement; shadow feasibility does not establish uptake.

openings.claim: An authoritative booking record with unique reservation identifiers and explicit confirmation of each change may reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.delta: Make each telephone or desk change traceable through confirmation and calendar copying.
openings.prediction: If ambiguous change handling causes conflicts, discrepancies and duplicate expectations should decline; persistent conflicts with matching records would weaken that explanation.
openings.probe: Pilot one authoritative paper record: log each change once, confirm room/time verbally with its identifier, update the online copy, and check desk key release against the master. Track disagreements, arrival expectations and total administration minutes across eight weeks, including pilot work.
assumptions: Staff can consult the master before confirming access.
Extra logging may exceed the two-hour administration target and must be measured.
